subject: proper sampling unit for stratified design

messages.author: 78b49e190792c945
messages.subject: proper sampling unit for stratified design
parts:
Hi Distance Samplers,

I'm working with some bird point transect data collected in oak woodlands. The
survey design was as follows: 91 points were clustered within 16 "Units"
representing either untreated or treated woodlands (treatment involved
understory removal), and the points were surveyed twice in each of two
consecutive years. Units averaged 21 hectares and were not physically connected
to each other. I'll ultimately need density estimates for several species in
each stratum (treated and untreated) in each year. This will likely require
stratum estimates to often be based on pooled detection functions due to small
numbers of detections per stratum.

The folks I'm working with are concerned that using the individual points as the
sampling unit amounts to pseudoreplication, and that perhaps data from all
points in a unit should be pooled, with "Unit" (n=16) as the sampling unit. The
encounter rates and density estimates don't differ when I use this approach,
but, as you would expect, the variances are much higher, often twice as high (CV
of 40+ versus 20+). This is true for global as well as stratum estimates.

So is this pooling necessary, I'm wondering? Or is it a bit overcautious,
statistically speaking?

Mark Faherty
Ecostudies Institute
Homestead, FL
USA
